extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and substantive requirements for petitions to revive abandoned patent applications, acceptance of late issue/publication fees, and related reply/fee/documentation obligations under 35 U.S.C., the PLTIA, and 37 CFR (especially 1.137).

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer as condition for granting untimely petition to withdraw holding of abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to withdraw the holding of abandonment may be treated on its merit unless accompanied by a terminal disclaimer under 37 CFR 1.321(a) and the required fee under 37 CFR 1.20(d). The period to be disclaimed is the terminal part of the term of any patent granted thereon... equivalent to the period between: (A) the date that is twelve months from the date of applicant’s filing or submission of correspondence with the Office, for which further action by the Office can reasonably be expected; and (B) the filing date of a grantable petition to withdraw the holding of abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies when a terminal disclaimer and fee must accompany a petition to withdraw a holding of abandonment and precisely how the disclaimed period is calculated. Applies when the Office conditions grant on such disclaimer.

rubrics_metrics.name: When terminal disclaimer should not be required (applications filed June 8, 1995–before May 29, 2000)
rubrics_metrics.description: In utility and plant applications filed on or after June 8, 1995, but before May 29, 2000, a terminal disclaimer should not be required as a condition of granting an untimely petition to withdraw the holding of abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPLA must be consulted if the holding of abandonment involves (A) appellate review by the PTAB; (B) an interference or derivation proceeding under 35 U.S.C. 135 (including suspensions due to such proceedings); or (C) sealed condition/prosecution suspended due to a secrecy order under 35 U.S.C. 181—because patent term extension/due diligence adjustments may need to be effected.

rubrics_metrics.name: When terminal disclaimer should not be required (applications filed on/after May 29, 2000)
rubrics_metrics.description: In utility and plant applications filed on or after May 29, 2000, a terminal disclaimer should not be required as a condition of granting an untimely petition to withdraw the holding of abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because patent term adjustment is automatically reduced under 37 CFR 1.704(c)(4) (and 1.704(a) where notice not received) for applications subject to AIPA provisions if a petition to withdraw is not filed within two months of the notice of abandonment or applicant failed to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to revive abandoned applications and accept delayed payments (35 U.S.C. 27 and 37 CFR 1.137)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may establish procedures to revive an unintentionally abandoned application, accept an unintentionally delayed payment of the fee for issuing each patent, or accept an unintentionally delayed response in reexamination proceedings. 37 CFR 1.137 provides for revival of abandoned applications or terminated/limited reexamination prosecution on the basis of unintentional delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets statutory/regulatory basis for petitions under 37 CFR 1.137; revival on the ground of 'unintentional delay' (PLTIA restored revival for unintentional standard).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required components of a petition under 37 CFR 1.137
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition under 37 CFR 1.137 requires: (A) the required reply (unless previously filed); (B) the petition fee as set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(m); (C) any terminal disclaimer (and fee) required pursuant to 37 CFR 1.137(d); and (D) a statement that the entire delay in filing the required reply from the due date until filing a grantable petition was unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may require additional information where there is a question whether the delay was unintentional. For petitions filed more than two years after abandonment, additional explanation establishing that the entire delay was unintentional is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: General definition of the 'required reply' for revival petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally, the required reply is the reply sufficient to have avoided abandonment, had such reply been timely filed. A petition for an extension of time under 37 CFR 1.136 is not required to be included with the reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The content of the required reply depends on the reason for abandonment (see specific types below). For nonprovisional applications abandoned after close of prosecution, an RCE may meet the required reply in certain situations per 37 CFR 1.114.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply for abandonment under 37 CFR 1.57(a) (failure to timely submit copy of specification/drawings)
rubrics_metrics.description: In an application abandoned under 37 CFR 1.57(a), the required reply must include a copy of the specification and any drawings of the previously filed application. A certified copy of the previously filed application may be required for an application filed by reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a certified copy is required and not filed within the later of four months from the filing date of the application or sixteen months from the filing date of the previously filed application, a petition including a showing of good and sufficient cause and the petition fee are required. See MPEP § 601.01(a), subsection III for more details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply for abandonment due to failure to pay the issue fee or publication fee
rubrics_metrics.description: In an application abandoned for failure to timely pay the issue fee, the required reply must include the issue fee (and any required publication fee). For publication-fee abandonment, the required reply must include payment of the publication fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under PLTIA and 35 U.S.C. 151, the notice of allowance specifies the sum (issue + any publication fee) to be paid within three months; the issue fee due with the petition is the dollar amount specified in the notice of allowance. An applicant may change entity status for the petition fee but must pay the issue/publication fee in the dollar amount specified in the notice of allowance. Filing a continuing application without payment of the issue fee is not an acceptable reply for applications abandoned for failure to pay the issue fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply for abandonment due to failure to provide required drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: For an application abandoned for failure to provide required drawings, a petition to revive will be dismissed unless the required drawings are filed before or with the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing the drawings is a strict precondition to granting revival in such cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply for abandonment for failure to reply to a non-final action
rubrics_metrics.description: The required reply to a non-final action may be either: (A) an argument or amendment under 37 CFR 1.111; or (B) the filing of a continuing application under 37 CFR 1.53(b) (or a CPA under 1.53(d) for design applications). The petition may be granted if the proposed reply appears to be bona fide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The grant of a petition is not a determination that any reply under 1.111 is complete. After revival, the examiner may find the reply deficient and give a 2-month shortened statutory period under 37 CFR 1.135(c) to correct errors; extensions under 1.136(a) are permitted. Failure to correct leads to abandonment again.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply for abandonment for failure to reply to a final action
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply under 37 CFR 1.113 to a final action must include a request for continued examination (RCE) under 37 CFR 1.114 or cancellation of, or appeal from, the rejection of each rejected claim. Thus, the required reply must be one of: (A) a Notice of Appeal and appeal fee; (B) an amendment under 37 CFR 1.116 that cancels all rejected claims or otherwise places the application in condition for allowance; (C) filing an RCE accompanied by a submission meeting 37 CFR 1.111 and the requisite fee (for certain utility/plant apps); or (D) filing a continuing application (or CPA for design).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a Notice of Appeal is filed as the reply, the Director will set the time period under 37 CFR 41.37 for the appeal brief in the decision granting the petition. The Office of Petitions normally routes proposed amendments under 1.116 to the Technology Center to determine whether the amendment places the application in condition for allowance before granting revival. Examiners should annotate replies that are 'OK to enter upon revival'; otherwise they complete form PTOL-303 to advise denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply for abandonment for failure to file an appeal brief
rubrics_metrics.description: Where abandonment occurred because of failure to file an appeal brief, the required reply must be either: (A) an appeal brief in compliance with 37 CFR 41.37(c); (B) filing an RCE accompanied by a submission and requisite fee in compliance with 37 CFR 1.114 (for certain utility/plant apps); or (C) filing a continuing application (or CPA for design).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides alternative paths to revive when appeal-brief omission caused abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using an RCE as the required reply (conditions for acceptability)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an RCE is the reply filed pursuant to 37 CFR 1.137(b)(1), the submission accompanying the RCE must be a reply responsive within the meaning of 37 CFR 1.111 to the last Office action. Consideration of responsiveness is done without factoring in the 'final' status of such action; the submission may be a previously filed amendment after final or a statement incorporating by reference prior arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petition may be granted if the submission appears to be a bona fide attempt to provide a complete reply. After revival, the examiner may determine that the reply is lacking and send a 2-month shortened statutory period under 37 CFR 1.135(c) for correction; extensions under 1.136(a) permitted; failure to correct causes abandonment again.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office may require a continuing application or RCE where reply would place inordinate burden on Office
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may require the filing of a continuing application or an RCE (if prosecution prior to abandonment was closed) (or request for further examination under 37 CFR 1.129(a)) to meet the reply requirement where treating a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 or 1.113 would place an inordinate burden on the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exemplary circumstances: (A) application abandoned for an inordinate period of time; (B) application file contains multiple or conflicting replies to the last Office action; (C) the reply or replies submitted under 37 CFR 1.137(b)(1) are questionable as to compliance with 37 CFR 1.111 or 1.113.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonpublication request + foreign filing notification requirement and revival
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant makes a nonpublication request and then files a counterpart application in a foreign country or under a treaty that requires 18-month publication, the applicant must rescind the nonpublication request and notify the Office of such foreign filing within 45 days; failure to timely provide such notice results in abandonment under 35 U.S.C. 122(b)(2)(B)(iii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.137(f) provides that an application abandoned for failure to timely provide such notice is subject to revival under 1.137 if the delay was unintentional. The reply requirement of 1.137(c) is met by the notification, but filing a petition to revive will not stay any period for reply that may be running. Applicants may use form PTO/SB/64a to file a petition for revival under 37 CFR 1.137.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition fee requirement and refund policy (35 U.S.C. 41(a)(7) / 37 CFR 1.17(m))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office shall charge $1,700.00 on filing each petition for revival of an abandoned application (and for related delayed fees/claims/extensions) (35 U.S.C. 41(a)(7)). The Director may refund any part of the fee in exceptional circumstances as determined by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The phrase 'on filing' means the petition fee is due on filing (not merely grant). The Office will not refund the petition fee regardless of whether the petition is dismissed or denied (unless exceptional circumstances). The Office will not reach the merits of any petition lacking the requisite petition fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unintentional delay standard and candor/duty considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office usually relies on the applicant’s duty of candor and good faith and accepts the statement that 'the entire delay...was unintentional' without requiring further information in the vast majority of petitions under 37 CFR 1.137. Practitioners are obligated under 37 CFR 11.18 to inquire into the underlying facts when providing this statement. An inappropriate statement may have adverse effects when attempting to enforce any resulting patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extended delay (>2 years from date of abandonment) raises questions and will usually trigger a requirement for additional information to establish that the entire delay was unintentional. A deliberately chosen course of action that led to abandonment is not 'unintentional' and cannot be retroactively characterized as such (citing In re Application of G and In re Maldague). Inappropriate statements have led to findings of inequitable conduct and unenforceability (e.g., Lumenyte Int’l Corp. v. Cable Lite Corp.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for additional information for petitions filed more than two years after abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: Any applicant filing a petition to revive an abandoned application more than two years after the date of abandonment must provide additional explanation of the circumstances surrounding the delay that establishes that the entire delay was unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office requires this to ensure sufficient information of facts and circumstances surrounding the entire delay to support a conclusion of unintentionality. The Office is almost always satisfied by applicant or representative statements explaining the cause of the delay (accompanied at most by copies of correspondence), except where extended delay exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment specifics when reviving for failure-to-pay issue/publication fee (amounts tied to notice of allowance)
rubrics_metrics.description: The issue fee due with the petition to revive is the issue fee dollar amount specified in the notice of allowance. If the notice of allowance also specified a publication fee, that publication fee must also be paid in the dollar amount specified on the notice of allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may change entity status when filing the petition to revive and pay the petition fee in the new entity status amount, but the issue/publication fee must be paid in the amount specified in the notice of allowance. This contrasts with timely-filed issue fee payments where payment corresponds to the newly established entity status amount. See MPEP § 1303 reproduction of 'HOW TO REPLY TO THIS NOTICE.'
